prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” truck-accident lawyer for everyone — the right attorney depends on your case details (severity, fault issues, injuries, commercial carrier involvement) and what you need (settlement vs. trial, medical/rehab advocacy, willingness to take on big trucking companies). Instead of a single name, here’s a practical way to find the best lawyer in Dallas for your truck accident case and how to pick between top candidates.

What to look for
- Substantial truck-accident experience (not just general car-crash work). Truck cases involve FMCSA rules, logbooks, hours-of-service, cargo, and carrier liability.
- Trial experience and a history of taking cases to verdict when needed.
- Resources to investigate and hire experts (accident reconstructionists, medical experts).
- Good track record of settlements/verdicts in commercial vehicle cases.
- Clear fee structure (contingency fee, percentage, who pays costs if you lose).
- Positive client reviews and no serious disciplinary history (check Texas Bar).
- Communication style and accessibility you’re comfortable with.

Where to search and vet attorneys
- Texas State Bar website (verify license and disciplinary history).
- Super Lawyers (Texas — Dallas area) and Martindale-Hubbell (peer reviews).
- Local trial lawyer groups (Texas Trial Lawyers Association) and plaintiff-oriented associations.
- Client review sites (Avvo, Google) — use reviews as one data point, not the only one.
- Ask friends/family or other local attorneys for referrals.

Questions to ask in a consultation (bring a short summary of the crash and your medical records)
- How much of your practice is commercial/truck accident work?
- How many truck cases have you handled in Dallas County? How many went to trial?
- Do you have experience with FMCSA regulations, logbook analysis, black box/ELD data?
- Which experts would you use and how are those costs handled?
- What is your fee and who pays expert/filing costs?
- What is a realistic timeline and likely range of recovery for my case?
- Can you provide references from recent truck-accident clients?

Practical next steps right now
- Preserve evidence: photos, dashcam, medical records, police report, contact info for witnesses.
- Do not give a recorded statement to the insurer without a lawyer.
- Seek prompt medical care and keep all records/receipts.
- Get at least 2–3 consultations (many are free) to compare approaches.

If you want, I can:
- Help draft an email/phone script to contact attorneys.
- Walk through any names you already have and list what to check about each.
- Suggest how to evaluate fee proposals and retainer agreements.

Tell me whether you’d like referrals (I can’t browse the web right now, but I can show how to find and vet top Dallas firms and prepare questions/email templates).
